title: Relative pronouns
blurb: Who, which and what: words that join a noun to a clause that tells you more about it.
hero_html:
STAGE 3 · UNIT 4

The one who, the thing which

A relative pronoun joins a noun to a short clause about it: "the student who passed". It is fixed, and it never stands alone.

الَّذِي

blocks.html: Tip: Spelling: الَّذِي، الَّتِي، الَّذِينَ are written with one ل and a shadda. اللَّاتِي and اللَّوَاتِي are written with two.

src.text: Spelling: {الَّذِي}، {الَّتِي}، {الَّذِينَ} are written with one {ل} and a shadda. {اللَّاتِي} and {اللَّوَاتِي} are written with two.

blocks.html: All of these are fixed. الَّذِينَ ends like a plural, but it never changes: it is الَّذِينَ in rafʿ, naṣb and jarr. الَّذِي and الَّتِي always end in a long ī.

blocks.html: 2A relative needs a clause after it

src.text: A relative needs a clause after it

blocks.html: الَّذِي alone means nothing. The clause after it completes its meaning. This clause is called the صِلَةٌ.

src.text: {الَّذِي} alone means nothing. The clause after it completes its meaning. This clause is called the {صِلَةٌ}.

blocks.html:
جَاءَ الطَّالِبُ الَّذِي نَجَحَ.
The student who passed came.
The ṣila is نَجَحَ.
هَذِهِ هِيَ الْبِنْتُ الَّتِي كَتَبَتِ الدَّرْسَ.
This is the girl who wrote the lesson.
The ṣila is كَتَبَتِ الدَّرْسَ.
الْكِتَابُ الَّذِي عَلَى الْمَكْتَبِ جَدِيدٌ.
The book which is on the desk is new.
The ṣila is a place phrase: عَلَى الْمَكْتَبِ.
خَرَجَ الرِّجَالُ الَّذِينَ جَلَسُوا فِي الْمَسْجِدِ.
The men who sat in the mosque went out.
The ṣila is جَلَسُوا فِي الْمَسْجِدِ.

items.ar: هَذِهِ هِيَ الْبِنْتُ الَّتِي كَتَبَتِ الدَّرْسَ.
items.en: This is the girl who wrote the lesson.
The book which is on the desk is new.
items.note: The ṣila is a place phrase: {عَلَى الْمَكْتَبِ}.

items.ar: خَرَجَ الرِّجَالُ الَّذِينَ جَلَسُوا فِي الْمَسْجِدِ.
items.en: The men who sat in the mosque went out.

blocks.html: Tip: The ṣila has a small link back to the noun. Often it is hidden in the verb (نَجَحَ "he passed"). Sometimes it is an attached pronoun: الطَّالِبُ الَّذِي بَيْتُهُ قَرِيبٌ "the student whose house is near".

src.text: The ṣila has a small link back to the noun. Often it is hidden in the verb ({نَجَحَ} "he passed"). Sometimes it is an attached pronoun: {الطَّالِبُ الَّذِي بَيْتُهُ قَرِيبٌ} "the student whose house is near".

blocks.html: 3Choose by the noun before it

src.text: Choose by the noun before it

blocks.html: Like an adjective, the relative follows a noun with ال and matches it: male or female, one or a group.

src.text: Like an adjective, the relative follows a noun with {ال} and matches it: male or female, one or a group.

blocks.html:
الْوَلَدُ الَّذِي فِي الْبَيْتِ
the boy who is in the house
One male: الَّذِي.
السَّاعَةُ الَّتِي عَلَى السَّرِيرِ
the watch which is on the bed
السَّاعَةُ is feminine: الَّتِي.
الْأَوْلَادُ الَّذِينَ خَرَجُوا
the boys who went out
A group of males: الَّذِينَ.
النِّسَاءُ اللَّاتِي خَرَجْنَ
the women who went out
A group of females: اللَّاتِي.

items.en: the boy who is in the house
the watch which is on the bed

blocks.html: Tip: Look at the verb in the ṣila too. It matches the relative: الَّذِي خَرَجَ، الَّتِي خَرَجَتْ، الَّذِينَ خَرَجُوا، اللَّاتِي خَرَجْنَ.

src.text: Look at the verb in the ṣila too. It matches the relative: {الَّذِي خَرَجَ}، {الَّتِي خَرَجَتْ}، {الَّذِينَ خَرَجُوا}، {اللَّاتِي خَرَجْنَ}.

blocks.html: Tip: After a noun without ال, Arabic leaves the relative out: جَاءَ طَالِبٌ نَجَحَ "A student who passed came."

src.text: After a noun without {ال}, Arabic leaves the relative out: {جَاءَ طَالِبٌ نَجَحَ} "A student who passed came."

blocks.html: 4مَنْ and مَا: question or relative?

src.text: مَنْ and مَا: question or relative?

blocks.html: مَنْ and مَا are also question words (unit 5). Look at the sentence. A question ends in ؟. A relative sits inside a normal sentence and means "the one who" or "what".

src.text: {مَنْ} and {مَا} are also question words (unit 5). Look at the sentence. A question ends in {؟}. A relative sits inside a normal sentence and means "the one who" or "what".

blocks.html:
مَنْ نَجَحَ؟
Who passed?
A question.
جَاءَ مَنْ نَجَحَ.
The one who passed came.
A relative. نَجَحَ is its ṣila.
مَا عَلَى الْمَكْتَبِ؟
What is on the desk?
A question.
اِقْرَأْ مَا عَلَى الْمَكْتَبِ.
Read what is on the desk.
A relative.

items.en: Read what is on the desk.

blocks.html: 5Its place in the sentence
A relative after a noun works like an adjective. It is fixed, so it cannot copy the ending. It copies the place of the noun before it.

src.text: A relative after a noun works like an adjective. It is fixed, so it cannot copy the ending. It copies the place of the noun before it.

blocks.html:
جَاءَ الطَّالِبُ الَّذِي نَجَحَ.
The student who passed came.
الطَّالِبُ is rafʿ, so الَّذِي is in the place of rafʿ.
شَكَرَ الْمُدِيرُ الطَّالِبَ الَّذِي نَجَحَ.
The principal thanked the student who passed.
الطَّالِبَ is naṣb, so الَّذِي is in the place of naṣb.
ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى الطَّالِبِ الَّذِي نَجَحَ.
I went to the student who passed.
الطَّالِبِ is jarr, so الَّذِي is in the place of jarr.

items.note: {الطَّالِبُ} is rafʿ, so {الَّذِي} is in the place of rafʿ.

items.en: The principal thanked the student who passed.
items.note: {الطَّالِبَ} is naṣb, so {الَّذِي} is in the place of naṣb.

items.en: I went to the student who passed.
items.note: {الطَّالِبِ} is jarr, so {الَّذِي} is in the place of jarr.

blocks.html: Tip: مَنْ and مَا stand alone, so they have their own job. In جَاءَ مَنْ نَجَحَ, مَنْ is the doer: place of rafʿ.

src.text: {مَنْ} and {مَا} stand alone, so they have their own job. In {جَاءَ مَنْ نَجَحَ}, {مَنْ} is the doer: place of rafʿ.

blocks.html: 6Not fixed: اللَّذَانِ and اللَّتَانِ

The words for "the two who" change. اللَّذَانِ (two males) and اللَّتَانِ (two females) are flexible. In naṣb and jarr they become اللَّذَيْنِ and اللَّتَيْنِ. You learn them with the dual in Stage 4.

src.title: The words for "the two who" change
src.text: {اللَّذَانِ} (two males) and {اللَّتَانِ} (two females) are flexible. In naṣb and jarr they become {اللَّذَيْنِ} and {اللَّتَيْنِ}. You learn them with the dual in Stage 4.

blocks.html:
FormTwo malesTwo females
Rafʿاللَّذَانِاللَّتَانِ
Naṣb and jarrاللَّذَيْنِاللَّتَيْنِ

In short

  1. الَّذِي one male or thing, الَّتِي one female or thing, الَّذِينَ males, اللَّاتِي / اللَّوَاتِي females.
  2. مَنْ "the one who" for people, مَا "what" for things.
  3. A relative needs a ṣila (صِلَةٌ) after it: الَّذِي نَجَحَ.
  4. Match the noun before it. The relative takes the place of that noun: rafʿ, naṣb or jarr.
  5. اللَّذَانِ and اللَّتَانِ are not fixed. They wait for Stage 4.
